utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours, good morning to everybody. For the Prosecution, Sureta Chana, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, and case manager Andres Vatter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Benjamin. Can we have the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel; Stefane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Alexis Demirdjian, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For today, Wednesday, we will continue with our proceedings. The Chamber bids good morning to all those present, the representatives of the Prosecution, the Defence counsel, the accused, as well as all the staff of this courtroom. Today we have an investigator as a witness. But before that, the Chamber would like to convey to the parties, and especially to the Prosecution, the following: It has to do with the contested documents. In order to ensure effective and as speedy as possible examination of the contested documents, because the Chamber needs to render a written decision in this connection, the Chamber would like to obtain from the Prosecution some clarifications concerning the problem of missing translations and missing documents. The Chamber, in its oral decision of the 17th of May, 2004, requested that the Prosecution provide the contested documents that are still missing from the binder, as well as the accompanying translations. For this purpose, the legal officer provided to the Prosecution a list, which is not exhaustive, an incomplete list of the documents lacking, so as to assist the Prosecutor in its task. In its filing of the 8th of June, a memo of the Prosecution following the oral decision of the 17th of May, the Prosecution indicated that the translations that were lacking had been provided to the Chamber, as they were received from the translation services. Regarding the war diaries and logbooks, the Prosecutor specified that their translation will probably not be available before the 30th of June, 2004. The Prosecutor also added, and I quote, that: "They will continue to monitor the development of the situation and will keep the Trial Chamber and the Defence informed on a regular basis." Since then, the Chamber has indeed received a certain number of the documents lacking, as well as translations, on the 4th and the 10th of June, 2004. Those documents complemented the package of contested documents, and the Chamber thanks the Prosecutor for providing them with these documents. However, it would appear that the binders are still not complete. It would therefore be desirable at this stage of the proceedings that the Prosecution inform, as soon as possible, the Chamber of the progress achieved since the last provision of documents, and in particular, with respect to the most voluminous documents, and in this connection, the contested documents 585 and 586, which are the files of military investigations of the court in Zenica. The Chamber would also like the Prosecution to inform the Chamber of the required time that will be required for the completion of the translations. As the Prosecution is aware, the closing of its case cannot legally take place before all the documents have been tendered and all the exhibits have been translated. We cannot have a closing of the case legally before the totality of the documents and exhibits have been filed and given an exhibit number. As the Prosecution is aware, we still have a few witnesses left, but theoretically, we should complete the hearing of witnesses not later than the beginning of July. It would be paradoxical to have to wait for several weeks, even several months, for the translations to reach us. Perhaps it would be desirable for the Prosecution to provide us a complete overview, which could be compiled as follows: A list of the documents that are still lacking, which were identified from the beginning; the list of the translations that are lacking, of all the documents. Another column in which, document by document, the date would be indicated when those documents or translations were sent to us. And then a final column in which you would indicate when the lacking documents or translations would be provided, indicating a date, if possible, when we would have those documents. Ms. Benjamin, I don't know whether you are in a position to respond now. Perhaps as the totality of these problems have been managed by Mr. Mundis, we are somewhat nervous, because we see that we still have either documents or translations lacking. Perhaps you need to consult with him. Do you wish to intervene or would you prefer Mr. Mundis to respond on the basis of the transcript of my words?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can assist you with what's before me now, but certainly, as you quite rightly said, Mr. Mundis has been the person who has been tasked with this assignment, and I prefer him to go into the complete details with respect to the list and what times you're going to get the balance. But as we speak, there's a bundle ready for the Court this morning. Yes, a bundle of translations that is ready to be delivered this very morning. With respect to Exhibits 585 and 586, they have been put on CD-ROMs and the Defence has theirs, and I think at the end of the first break we would be able to give hard copies to the Judges, with respect to 585 and 586. That's basically what I have now. Sorry, Mr. President. I'm told by the case manager that the logs and the war diaries, we have been given the date 30th of June when they should be ready and a few at the beginning of July. So I would deliver the ones we have now, the hard copy later, and I'll certainly get messages out to the people that are in charge with respect to the exhibits. I apologise on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Regarding the lacking documents and translations, does the Defence wish to comment on this subject at all? No comments. No observations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we shall wait for Mr. Mundis to bring us up to date, and also you're telling us that some documents will be provided to us by the 30th of June, when we will have documents 585 and 586. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: That's my understanding, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us bring in the witness who is on the schedule for today. Madam Usher, will you go and fetch the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we bring in the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The witness who gave evidence before with respect to the sketches and the photographs was a protected witness, so it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. means that these documents are under seal. And I propose something to the Registry, and I think they were in agreement with it, that we would have to cover the initial of the witness who gave testimony under protective measures with respect to the things. So if it pleases the Court, maybe that's the procedure we should adopt. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence obviously can only support such a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But this is also an occasion for us to say, before the witness comes in, that the documents that we attached and which the Trial Chamber has admitted in connection with the witness who testified last week as a protected witness, that those documents with his signature be placed under seal. When a decision was made on their admission, we didn't make this point, that is, that all documents signed by that witness should also be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Those are the documents that you filed yesterday; is that right? Very well. So, Mr. Registrar, the documents that may relate to that witness, which he marked, should be placed under seal if the name of the witness appears on the document. And to avoid any contamination, they must be placed under seal. But we'll deal with that problem later on. The Chamber takes note of the point made. So let us bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. Let me check that you are hearing my words, translated into your language, at least into English that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have been called by the Prosecution to testify before this Tribunal. Before asking you to read the solemn declaration, could you please give me your name, date and place of birth, and nationality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Mika Tauru. I was born on 17 of March, 1963, and I'm a Finnish citizen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Currently I'm detective sergeant working in the homicide unit of Helsinki criminal police in Helsinki, Finland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're a Finnish police officer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before taking up this position in the Finnish police force, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I worked here as an investigator for three years since 1999 until 2002, and I've been working as a police since 1986 in Finland. Sorry, 1985 in Finland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you testified before in this Tribunal, or is this the first time that you're appearing as a witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you testified in any other court of an international one, but a national one, about the events that took place in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993, or is this the first time you are testifying about them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you're going to testify, you need to take the solemn declaration, and would you kindly read it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please be seated. Before giving the floor to the Prosecution for them to put questions to you, I need to provide you with some information regarding these proceedings. For this Chamber, you're the first investigator coming to testify, though the trial started in December last year, hence the importance of your testimony. Also, as you have sworn to tell the truth, the whole truth, that excludes all forms of false testimony. And as you know, in your country and any country in the world, and also in this Tribunal, perjury can be punished by a fine or a prison sentence. Of course, I draw attention to another point but which shouldn't apply to you, and that is if a witness refuses to answer a particular question, he may do so if he thinks that this could subsequently incriminate him. In this very specific case, the rules of this Tribunal envisage that the witness may be compelled to answer, yet he is guaranteed a form of immunity from punishment, where's in some countries, like the United States, such immunity is provided by the prosecutor. According to our rules, it is the Chamber that gives this immunity. But of course in principle, it shouldn't apply to you. You will have to answer, as you know, questions within the examination-in-chief, which will be conducted by a representative of the Prosecution who is seated to your right. As you know, the questions are of a neutral nature and not leading in any sense. However, the Defence, who are on your left, may put any questions to you, either to verify your credibility or to provide additional information on the context. And they may put to you questions of quite a different nature from those of the Prosecution. At the end of that stage, the Prosecution may have additional questions. Also, the Judges in front of you may ask you questions. In view of your position as investigator, you can envisage that we will have questions for you regarding your work, regarding what you did, the way in which you carried out the instructions of the Prosecution in your investigations, and we will have questions for you which we consider to be useful for a better understanding of this case, and especially of the way in which you worked on the ground. But that will come at the end of the questions of both parties. It's quite possible that we will not have any questions for you, if the parties put the same questions to you. We will only have questions to fill in any missing gaps. So, in summary, that is how the proceedings will evolve. Being a specialist for investigations, you know that your answers have to be clear and precise so that the Judges may fully understand the meaning and the gist of your answers. If the questions appear to you to be complicated or unclear, ask the party putting them to you to rephrase them. And the Chamber will intervene to assist you should the need arise. Without further ado, I shall give the floor to the Prosecution for their examination-in-chief. Madam Benjamin, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Ms. Henry-Benjamin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tauru. You already indicated your profession at the time period which we're going to speak about when you were at the Tribunal. As a result of your role as an investigator, did you at any time perform a mission with respect to the time period of the indictment in this case, which is January 1993 to March 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: During the years that I worked here, I had many missions to Bosnian and Croatia and also to some other countries, and probably something like 20 to 25 missions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Our mission here this morning is relating particularly to your mission in reference to the indictment period here, which is January 1993 to March 1994. And as I said already, did you have cause to go on a mission with respect to that period?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you went on the mission?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Are you talking about the mission in April 2002?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you now explain to us what the mission entailed. What was your role and what duties did you carry out on the mission? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: The purpose of the mission was to record all the crime scenes that feature in our indictment, to get them professionally photographed and videotaped, and also part of the mission was to take part of -- at least three members of our trial team to get them familiarised with the crime scenes, take them around all the crime sites and crime scenes, and probably the most important thing that we're going to be -- according to my understanding we'll be handling here today was the recording of the destroyed villages in Central Bosnia, the destroyed Croat villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Along with you on this mission, were there any other parties?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: There was two -- there were two Dutch crime scene specialists and one other investigator from our team, Mr. Tom Parker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have a photographer on the -- in the party?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. There was two Dutch policemen who were crime scene specialists, so they took the photographs and videotaped the sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the pictures being taken, you indicated to us that you drew sketches. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prepared sketches?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes. In the beginning of this mission, after I flew to Sarajevo on 6th of April, the following day, on 7th of April, I started preparing sketches of the destroyed villages, together with our local contact person in (Redacted) And before that I had informed him about this, our planned mission, about one month earlier, that we wanted to get all the destroyed houses recorded in those villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Sir, Mr. Registrar, would you prepare an order for me, please. It's a name that you have just mentioned should not be mentioned. You said -- you say Mr. X. You should say Mr. X.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Perhaps to make it easy, maybe you can just -- don't mention names of any of the parties. You know, you went to the photographer, you went to the forensic specialist or whatever. Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak a little more loudly or approach the microphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you -- before the interruption, you began to tell us that you prepared sketches. And could you tell us how you prepared these sketches. Did you have them in particular groups? How did you do these sketches?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: We proceeded village by village, and before this actual mission was started, like I mentioned earlier, I contacted our contact person in Bosnia and told him about the plan that we were planning such a mission and gave him the criteria, what we were after, the time period regarding each of those villages, and also which kind of damage we requested to be recorded. It was agreed here within the team that we would not take any houses which only carried some bullet holes. There had to be significant damage. And one thing that was also mentioned to this local contact person was that any buildings which had been destroyed during that period in question but had been later reconstructed would not be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that the sketches you provided, were they sketches that concerned only destroyed houses during the period of the indictment, the time period?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on those sketches, we would not be seeing houses that were destroyed after; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, could we --

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown P81, please. On the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could perhaps put it on the ELMO, provided that the names have been concealed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Maybe for us to save time and to do them together as a bundle, could you tell the Court -- you indicated that you had taken pictures after the sketches; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Pictures of the sketches?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Did you take pictures of the sites after you drew the sketches?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you match your sketches with your pictures?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interests of time, maybe we can let him have his pictures and his sketches so he can just go through one -- same bundle at the same time. So could we have -- yes. Could we give him the -- on the ELMO, please. And the sketch. We could probably put them lengthways. Can they go like this? Lengthways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tauru, could you look at the documents before you and first let us start with the sketch. Could you explain to the Court what is -- what are you representing there, please.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: I don't really see well the front right-hand corner there. So first there is this marking Ovnak 1, meaning that this was the first sketch prepared of Ovnak village. And then there's a list of names, starting from number 1 until 24, as far as I can see. And then those -- all these numbered houses are marked on the sketch along the road leading through the village. And there are some buildings which have been marked with dotted line. That means that those were not actually destroyed houses. They were just marked there for the purpose of helping me in recognising the right building from the aerial photograph, which was taken later. And there's a north arrow also below the name,. And there's also up there is a mosque mark which is kind of an orientation point as well, not meaning that the mosque was destroyed, just as a landmark. And I think -- I don't see that below there should be also - if you take this one out - there should be the -- there should be also the exact coordinates of the certain reference point which is marked with X on the left-hand side of number 20, a couple of centimetres to the left, there's an X marked in the one junction, and that's the place where I took the reference point and marked the coordinates with a GPS device.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these sketches, what was the purpose of preparing the sketches? If you notice that there's no scale or anything on this. There are no representative of street names or anything. Could you tell us what is the purpose of doing these sketches?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: The purpose of doing these sketches was just to help me later on to transfer the information from these sketches to the actual aerial photographs, so that I would be able -- be in a position to locate the exact locations of each of those destroyed houses and other buildings. That's why they're not in a scale or anything. It was just like a tool for me to prepare the final product.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you consider the pictures as the final product? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you look at the corresponding picture to the sketch that you've just shown us. Could you tell us how you related this to that sketch and where we are.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Those numbers, unfortunately, I don't see really the numbers, just so small -- a small copy of the actual big photograph that was done. It was much bigger in size, much bigger than this A-4 size, so unfortunately we don't obviously have those available, so I don't really see the numbers. But in the original you can see them much better. But anyway, how it was done, you can see the red arrows pointing so certain buildings and also blue arrows. And the red arrows are pointing to real buildings, meaning warm houses, houses that the people lived in. And the red -- sorry. The blue ones are pointing to cold Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. houses, meaning outbuildings, garages, sheds, barns, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, it seems to me that it's not coming through very clear on the ELMO, so I wonder if the witness can be presented with a still copy on his desk so he can -- thanks.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Okay. So, for example, if you take a look at the house number 2, red arrow pointing to a building, actual building where people used to live in, and below that there's a blue arrow with the number 2 on it, pointing to a certain outbuilding belonging to this same house, the same owner than the actual house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what are those arrows indicating? What are they telling us? What did you see there? Was something wrong with that house? What is ...

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Those are destroyed houses, destroyed buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you need to tell the Trial Chamber. So tell us, you know, what the arrows are and ...

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: So the arrows are pointing to destroyed houses and outbuildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The blue signifies a different thing to the red or ...

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. Blue is it an outbuilding, shed, garage, barn, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the red is?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Red is a building where people used to live in, warm building, with the warm colour red. And the blue is a kind of cold colour, meaning that there was no heating, it was just an outbuilding. That's the logic behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we look at picture number 2 in the bundle. Yes. Could you carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: The same story. In this picture there are only red arrows, meaning that there are only real houses with people living in that have been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from what angle would you say that these pictures were taken?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: This was taken from totally just opposite the -- not exactly. I think the picture number Ovnak 1 was taken from south or south-west, and this is taken from north, as far as I can recall. The same area, anyway, the same village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So let's look at the sketches that you have and picture number 2, for example. How do you reconcile for us the sketch with the picture? How does -- how did it work? You should have 58, 59 in the bundle, 60. There should be three sketches in the bundle.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that if you talk about sketch number 1 of Ovnak and the picture number 1 of Ovnak, they don't necessarily cover exactly the same areas. So in one picture, like in this Ovnak number 2, there are some houses which are not in the sketch number 2. So it's a mixture of different sketches. Because it was impossible for many -- on many occasions to get all the houses which are on a certain sketch, to get under one photograph. So that's why it's like combined information from different sketches. But the main thing is that every single house which has been listed was destroyed is in some of these photographs that were taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence, then, that the way the bundles are put, the sketches with the photographs, are not necessarily what you wanted to achieve? Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: No. No. No. What I'm saying is that when I went on the ground, I went to certain part of the village and I recorded some part of the village, wrote down and wrote the sketch of that area, but later when we took the aerial photographs, they were not exactly from the same group of houses that I have listed in the sketch. So I tried to make the sketches so -- or the aerial photographs so that there would be as more number as possible as the aerial photographs as possible, so that I was able to combine the information from many of the sketches in one photograph. Otherwise -- because we took -- all together we took 176 aerial photographs. It was a big job to kind of choose the right ones which will be used as those photographs where I then transferred the information from the sketches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- I am a bit confused. I'm going to ask you this now: What was the purpose of taking the aerial photographs, of drawing the sketches? What did you want to support? What was the purpose of this? What were you told that you needed these photographs for and these sketches?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: The sketches were drawn for the purpose of getting the exact locations of those buildings on the ground. The houses were marked. All the landmarks were marked. The junctions, little bridges or whatever, paths there were, in order later on to be in a position to mark them on the aerial photographs, which were later taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you will agree with me when I say that there's no scale on these things?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: There's no scale. It was just a tool for me to be able to put those buildings on the aerial photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how are we going to explain to this Trial Chamber, and for my own knowledge too, that when you say that this is Ovnak 1, how do we really know that that is Ovnak 1, and how are we going to deal with this? Because I'm at a loss myself. What was the plan? How are we going to deal with it?

In the middle of the sketch you will see the graveyard marked, and that graveyard is the one on the right top-hand corner of the picture. And the houses are marked from 45 to 49, consistent with the sketch. Next one.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: P88, please.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: I have a question. Donje Cukle, is it upper or lower Cukle? Does anybody know? It helps me a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is very interesting, because you're the author of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: There's upper and lower, and if I knew which one this was, it would be easier for me to ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe if you look at your sketch, it may be able to help you.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Okay. This is picture Donje Cukle number 1, and it's the sketch Donje Cukle number 1 as well, houses marked from 1 to 7 will be seen on the sketch as well. Next one, please. This is Donje Cukle number 2, and this has lots of houses from many different sketches, at least numbers 21 to 28 from sketch number Donje Cukle 3 are in this picture. Also from the sketch Donje Cukle 6, houses numbered from 11 to 17 are on this picture. And also sketch Donje Cukle number 2 has the houses numbered 17, 18, and 20 are on this picture. And the houses number 10 and below that on the right-hand corner are mentioned in the sketch number 5, Donje Cukle 5, houses numbered from 1 to 10. And I think that covers this picture. Next one, please. This is picture Donje Cukle number 3, and we have to have a sketch number Donje Cukle 4. We can see all these buildings marked on the sketch, from 29 until 38. They are on this sketch. Next one, please. Donje Cukle 4 is the picture, and Donje Cukle 4 is also the sketch with all these numbered houses, from 39 to 44. Next one, please. This is picture Donje Cukle number 5, and we have to have the Donje Cukle number 4 sketch, which has a school marked on it in the middle, and you can see also the school in the picture on the left-hand side of house number 21. These houses from 18 to 21 in the middle of the picture are from sketch Donje Cukle 3, and the houses from number 11 to 17 can be seen on sketch Donje Cukle 6. And this one building on the bottom left-hand corner, number 9, can be seen on Donje Cukle number 5 sketch. Next one, please. Donje Cukle number 6 is the picture, and the sketch is Donje Cukle number 4, with houses numbered from 23 to 40. And again, the school is on the left on the picture, and in the sketch it's above those houses. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: May the witness be shown P89, please.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. This is Gornji Cukle number 1, and the first -- there are also many houses on different sketches. And if we start from the left upper hand corner, there's house number 22, and that's marked on Gornji Cukle 1 sketch, houses number 22, 20, and 21, 19 as well. I don't see so clearly. And then in the same -- from the same sketch, we have houses numbered 16, 17, 15, and 14, coming towards the centre of the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps, Witness, if you look at the last bundle that we gave you, those sketches are clearer than the ones you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: These are pretty clear, it's just that there's so many houses and it's difficult to...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Because I'm not able to see clearly the numbers of the -- on the photo. But they must be from the sketch number 4, those houses in the middle of the picture, numbered from 1 to 15. Yes, exactly. That's the one. The next one, please. This is Gornji Cukle 2, is the picture, and those houses will be seen in sketch number Gornji Cukle 2, numbered 4 to 7. Next one, please. This is picture Gornji Cukle number 3, in brackets, Bare, and the sketch is Gornji Cukle 3, in brackets, Bare, Kovacica Kuce. And these houses, starting from number 1, from the left, are seen on the bottom of this Gornji Cukle 3 sketch, up until the number 14. Next one, please. This is picture Gornji Cukle number 4, Bare in brackets. It's the end of the same village. And those houses marked from 15 to 22 will be seen also in the sketch number 3 of Gornji Cukle. Next one, please. Gornji Cukle number 5 is the picture, in brackets, Bare. This is the most upper part of the village. And those houses numbered from 23 to 24 are in the top of that Gornji Cukle number 3 sketch. Next one, please. The picture is Gornji Cukle number 6, Kovacica Kuce in brackets, houses marked with numbers 24, I guess, or 5 - I don't see clearly. But anyway, they are in the same sketch, the Gornji Cukle number 3, on the left top corner. The next one, please. Gornji Cukle number 7 is the picture, in brackets, Novo Selo. And this is sketch number 4 of Gornji Cukle, in brackets, Novo Selo. The houses marked on the top of that sketch, from 1 to 3. Next one, please. Gornji Cukle number 8, in brackets, Novo Selo. The same sketch, Gornji Cukle number 4, houses from number 4 to number 8 are in this picture. The next one, please. Gornji Cukle number 9, in brackets, Novo Selo. The same sketch, Gornji Cukle number 4, houses from 9 to 15 are marked on this map, like also in the sketch. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. That's the end of the sketches and the pictures, Mr. Tauru.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question to you would be: You indicated to us that your mission was to take these pictures and to prepare the sketches, corresponding sketches. You had to have done some sort of investigations before you prepared the sketches. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I don't know if you're referring to the instructions I gave to the contact person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from that, what I'm trying to ask is: Did investigations with any particular group of people were done before the sketches were done and the pictures were taken?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't think I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to anybody on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Not other than the local contact that we had. And of course, we had been talking to some witnesses before regarding these incidents, and also after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the witnesses would have been the owners of these houses, or who would have been these witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: The witnesses were -- especially after this mission, they were the owners of those houses and the people who remained in the village after the village was taken over by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is your evidence that the pictures that were taken and the sketches that were drawn were pictures taken of houses which were damaged during the period of the indictment? Is it that?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes the examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Benjamin. Are the Defence counsel ready for their questions? Do they have any questions for the witness? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Bourgon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tauru.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe we know each other from your previous time at the Tribunal, but for the benefit of the transcript, let me introduce myself. I am accompanied this morning with my colleague, Mrs. Edina Residovic, as well as my colleague, Mr. Alexis Demirdjian, and my name is Stefane Bourgon. Together we represent General Hadzihasanovic. I only have a few questions for you this morning, and I guess I can simply proceed directly with my questions. If at any time there's a question that you do not understand, feel free to ask for further clarification and I will provide those to you. The first thing I would like to confirm, Mr. Tauru, is that you were an investigator with the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal from 1999 to the year 2002.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that during this time frame, you conducted or took part in approximately 20 to 25 investigation missions in many areas of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And today the specific mission that we are talking about in the course of your examination-in-chief is the result of a mission you conducted or took part in, in April of 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you confirm, Mr. Tauru, that the object of this mission, and I'm looking at the answers you provided to my colleague, but that the object of this mission was to record the crime scenes related to the indictment against General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also wanted to make professional photographs and videos of those crime scenes?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the object as well was to familiarise members of the Prosecution team with the crime scenes?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can I ask for a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] In response to a question asked by my colleague from the Prosecution, you mentioned that no houses destroyed after this period were recorded. I take it that the period you were referring to was the period of the indictment, which is from January of 1993 to February of 1994, so that no houses destroyed after 1994 would have been recorded. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I mean, from -- after January 1994, no after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course your -- the Witness ZI, on the basis of the guidelines that you provided him, he set out to identify the houses you were looking for, which he then provided you with some information, and according to his testimony, he also gave you his own sketches, which looked very much like yours. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: No. He didn't give me any of his sketches. He kept them by himself, and I asked him to keep them just in case they will be needed in a later stage. I only prepared my own sketches, based on the information I got from him. He still has those sketches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never used his sketches to prepare yours?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: I never took them from him. We had a look at them. We were comparing them. But he kept them and still has them, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question is quite simple: Simply if it was used -- if those sketches were used to produce yours.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you, in terms of the information you had to produce these sketches, you had, of course, the pictures which were taken after the mission, or at the end of the mission, and you had the information from Witness ZI; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you then proceeded to Sarajevo, which is the area where you, based on this information, produced your own sketches?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: No. I produced the sketches on the spot, in each village. We went to the village. I started to prepare my sketch. And after we finished, I finished with the sketch, we went to the next village. So I finished the sketch in the village. First we just wrote down the numbers of the buildings and I marked the buildings, and after we had marked all those buildings, we stopped and we started to write down the names of the owners. So house number 1, owner this and this, and house number 2, owner this and this, until all those houses had the owners marked on my sketch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all along, this was the information coming from Witness ZI that you included in those sketches so that you would have all the information when you returned to Sarajevo, because you mentioned returning to Sarajevo this morning. That's why I made reference to this.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. But it took many days to get those sketches done. It was not done in one day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you confirm that what you mentioned earlier, that these sketches were not drawn up to scale, because in fact they were only to be used as a tool to assist you in labelling the pictures, which were really your final product that you were looking for?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, as you mentioned, that these sketches, if someone were to try and use them, it would require a thorough knowledge of the area, due to the difficulty in reading the land in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. I would say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, nevertheless, these sketches that we have seen today, they are your sketches?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that those sketches basically represent the destruction, or the houses you were looking for, according to your criteria, at the time that you had requested them, which is the month, the specific month that you referred to, to Witness ZI?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would I be right in saying that you do not know how or in what context these houses were destroyed, and to be more specific, whether these houses were destroyed by mortar rounds, by grenades, by gunfire, by burning, or by any other means, and you do not have this information; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Well, I have them -- I don't have them listed anywhere, but I have taken or we have taken photographs of every single house that has been listed here. But when I gave the test to our contact person to find the information regarding these villages, it was only a question of, you know, how many houses and who are the owners, and not that exactly how was this house, this particular house destroyed and how about this one. So on the spot then and they all been, you know, recorded on the -- by photographing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By photographing.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: From aerial photographs and also on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not -- you can confirm that you do not have information which was provided to you by Witness ZI concerning exactly how these houses were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: No, not during that mission. But after that, we decided that we will have to take more witnesses who will be able to testify about the incidents and what happened in the villages. So during this process when he went to the villages, he recognised many good witnesses who had stayed behind and had the knowledge of this, so later on during our mission, the same mission that I took this contact person's statement, we took many statements from the witnesses who were able to tell what happened actually in the villages after they were attacked and who did the damage and how was the damage done and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you, Mr. Tauru, would have nothing to add to what these witnesses would come and say in Court?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: No. They have much better knowledge than I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And actually, you do not have any information which you could provide us as to exactly who committed the damage on these houses?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could not provide us with any specific information as to exactly when these houses were destroyed other than in those periods, those months that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should simply like to point out that I didn't put any question to this witness that was addressed yesterday regarding the participation of the witness in an inquiry in Sarajevo. I preferred to wait for the Judges to put their questions and then see whether I have anything additional to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does the other Defence team have any questions for this witness as part of the cross-examination? Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. [Previous translation continues]... questions asked by Mr. Bourgon, Your Honours, we have no additional questions on behalf of Mr. Kubura for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has the Prosecution any re-examination before the Judges ask their questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Tauru, we are going to ask you a few questions which will focus on your work as an investigator on the spot through the sketches that you made. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my first question is: When you said that you were a police officer, so according to my calculations, you were 36 years old at the time, so you were an experienced police officer, and you told us --

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... age. I was a bit older than 36. But anyway. Born in 1963, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my calculations, that is 36. But anyway, that's a minor detail. The purpose of my question was not your age, but rather the way in which you worked. You told us that you went on 20 to 26 missions. But before leaving on mission, what would you receive as instructions from the OTP as to the way in which you should conduct your inquiries? Did you have carte blanche, you were free to do what you wanted, or did you have very precise guidelines as to the way in which you should act? Because if there is a police investigation, there's always the head of the investigation who will determine the modalities. So could you tell us, the Chamber, how you proceeded when conducting your investigations.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to point out that all the guidelines particularly were made already here in The Hague, together with the senior trial attorney, Ekkehard Withopf, we discussed this issue, how we are going to do this mission, and we agreed to do it exactly the same way that it's been explained here for a couple of times already. So he made a decision about the time frame that it's going to be exactly the calendar month that each particular village was attacked in 1993 or 1994, also that we wouldn't record any of the reconstructed houses which have been -- even though that they have been destroyed during the period in question, and also that we wouldn't take any small damage, like bullet holes or just something minor damage to the house. It has to be significant damage. And also we discussed about the role of the -- how we're going to do it with the Dutch crime scene specialists. We agreed that we would not videotape those destroyed buildings, that we would take the aerial photographs, and we took them all together, 176 photos of those ten villages. And we then took photographs on the ground of each of those destroyed villages so that -- each of destroyed houses so that we had the whole building. We took one from the south, one from the northern side, so that we had covered the whole building, or from east and west, and so on. And from some of the outbuildings, we took only one, if it was not that necessary, or important, that building, just small ruins, just one picture was enough. So this was the way we proceeded. And later on, after preparing the sketches and taking the aerial photographs, I returned to The Hague and worked on those aerial photographs. I wanted to pick up the best photographs to cover the villages. Out of those 176, I picked up 42, I guess, and transferred the information from the sketches. How I did it was that I marked with my own pen, either red or blue pen, and then the Dutch police officers came back and picked all the pictures, and they made the final board actually by doing -- making the arrows by computer. And that's the pictures you have with you today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, you were on the spot, following instructions given by the OTP, and you were accompanied on this mission by two Dutch specialists who assisted you.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes. They assisted me after I had taken already the sketches. When making the sketches, I was working only with the contact person and the following week came the Dutch crime scene specialists, and they took the aerial photos first and went through all the villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. So the contact person, Mr. X, so the contact person, who chose him? Was it you? Was it the OTP? Or someone told you, you should take Mr. X? Who chose this person?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Well, we had been making cooperation with this particular person for already some years, so he was always the person to contact when we had a mission, when we needed to get witnesses, so that's why he was an obvious choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So he had a -- he was a kind of privileged correspondent. Did you have any evidence regarding this gentleman that would guarantee that he would be objective? Because a serious and professional investigation would require such objectivity.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: I don't know too much about his background. I just know that he has been involved in some kind of intelligence organ in Bosnia. And I know that he's been living in the area for many years, all his life, probably, as far as I recall, and he knows also really well the area. So in many ways he was the right person. There was not even any discussion about getting somebody else, because he was our contact person and that's it. And he had been proven to be a really effective and reliable during all the previous missions that we'd been having and never let us down in anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But you are a professional investigator, and in this hall there are several persons who have engaged in investigations. Isn't it normal for an investigator to go on the spot, to meet someone by chance, a witness, and ask him questions, and then, on that basis, the basis is established for the investigation? Why did you choose a person selected in advance? Would you work in that way in your own country, or is this a specific method of procedure?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Well, it is a little bit specific method because you have to bear in mind that many of those villages that we are talking about today are totally empty. There are no people in those villages at all. So it doesn't make much sense to go there, since there's nobody. And in some villages, there are only Bosniaks and we don't want to go there and start talking about these incidents with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we saw a moment ago the aerial photographs. You identified all those photographs. It is true that on those photographs, we can't see anyone on the ground, at least from the height from which they were taken. Are you telling us that when you went there on the spot, there was no one there, or were there people around?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: In some of the bigger villages of course there were people around because people have returned to some of the villages, but some of the smaller ones like, you know, Dusina, Miletici, there's nobody there. But of course Grahovcici, Cukle they are huge villages and there are many people who have returned. So we also talked with them a little bit because of course they were interested in what we were doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. You're making a distinction between small villages and larger settlements. When you were there, did you have an interpreter with you?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes, we had an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you arrived in an important settlement, with many houses and some inhabitants. Within the framework of your activities as investigator, did you get in touch with inhabitants? Did you introduce yourself? Did you say that you had been sent there by the OTP in The Hague to make certain inquiries? Did you make such contact with the inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: I didn't really make any contacts by myself. The fact was that since our local contact person had been circling around the villages and gathering the information, most of the villages already have heard about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But what prevented you from getting in touch with those people yourself and asking them: You were there in 1993. What happened to you? Did you leave, et cetera. You didn't do any of that?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. That was not exactly the purpose of the mission. We had a really tight schedule and time frame. There were much more destroyed houses than we were expecting, and there was bad weather so that was also causing a lot of problems, and we all was kind of, you know, get our schedule, so that's why -- concentrating on what we were supposed to do on that particular mission. But if I may continue. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the purpose of an investigation, isn't it to collect evidence so as to be able to specifically define an offence made and to identify the perpetrator? Isn't that the basic function of any inquiry? The main purpose of any investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes. You can say that that's the main purpose, but it was not the main purpose of this particular mission. Like I said, there were really a huge number of houses, and if we stopped to talk with every single person who came by us, that would have totally ruined the whole schedule of this mission. But like I said earlier, based on the work done by our contact person, he developed many reliable and good and useful witnesses by going around in the villages, and those persons that he identified, they were then later, the following month, in June 2002, just, you know, the next mission we had to the area, those people were interviewed during that mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of this mission which took place in several stages, as an investigator and a police officer who was in charge of investigating buildings that were torched and destroyed, you know that technical elements involved in a fire, and usually it's necessary to have an expert who could say how a fire was set, whether it was with petrol, whether flame-thrower, et cetera, or was it the result of a shell or mortar shell or grenade. No one thought that you should be assisted by an expert on fires?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: No, we never thought about -- talked about this kind of issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In spite of the fact that you didn't think about this, you said that you took photographs of houses. What prevented you from making a personal note on the basis of each individual house, saying that this house that belongs to a certain person is as follows: You could say that at the ground floor a door was broken, that on the first floor you could see that there was certain damage, that the roof no longer existed? What prevented you from describing each individual house and establishing your personal conclusion, for example, saying that, "It seems to me the fire, the destruction was caused at such-and-such a period, at the same time as the events that we are investigating or after these events." No one had the idea of doing this? So rather than making sketches, et cetera, and then this note could have been attached to the photographs you had taken?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. That's something we never discussed. But, like you mentioned about fire, I was able to tell was it burned during the one particular month ten years ago or was it burned later, that's totally impossible to tell, no matter which kind of expert I would have taken with me. That I know for sure from my own experience. And we thought that taking aerial photographs plus taking separate photographs of each of those buildings from two different directions, showing exactly the damage, would do the thing. Anything else that was not anything that we planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You yourself, with the two Dutch policemen, the interpreter, and Mr. X, did you enter the houses that had been damaged? Did you go inside?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah, we went inside some of the buildings. Some of the buildings we went just close and took the photographs and then a little bit depended on the terrain, how it was and how many bushes there were around and how accessible the house was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the buildings that you entered, which were perhaps completely open, there was perhaps no door or it wasn't possible to shut it, did you discover houses that had been completely emptied, or were there in these houses clothes, items, pieces of furniture, televisions, fridges, or when entering these buildings, did you see that they were completely empty? What could you see upon entering such buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Basically all the houses were, 99 per cent sure I would say, they were totally empty or just some ruins, broken furniture or some window frames or whatever. Just rubbish, nothing valuable left. Because most of the -- in many cases, after the village was taken over by the BH army, also some sort of looting took place in most of the times, and then all the valuables have been removed as soon as possible from the houses. So there was nothing valuable left. And we discussed -- we discussed also about them possibly taking photographs from inside the houses, but before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But why do you say that it was the BH army that had taken everything and that had engaged in looting? You said so spontaneously. But what are the grounds for your claim?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: I never said that the BiH army looted the houses. I said that the villages and houses were looted after the BiH army took over them. I didn't say that the army looted the houses. Of course there are also civilians involved in these kind of issues, but I never said that the BiH army did that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there's an error in the transcript, you spontaneously said that it was the BH army. Now you are telling us something else. So I take note of that. You say that there was nothing left in these houses. Was there nothing left because fire had destroyed everything or because everything had been taken out, or items of value had been taken out in an organised manner, or was the scene such that one could assume that the fact that houses were empty was the result of destruction? What would your conclusion be on the basis of what you could see at these relevant sites?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: It's difficult to say what caused the damage and how the items were broken, but just as an example to show you that the looting didn't only happen right after the attack. I remember visiting Miletici, probably in 2000 for the first time, and I specifically remember one particular house that we took some photographs, and the following time I went there, the next time I went there was maybe one year later and it looked totally different. So it looks like, you know, that even nowadays, whatever might be left there, people are still going around and trying to find something and taking stuff out of the buildings, whatever might be left. So it's really difficult to say what happened and how they happened and who did it, other than those persons who were present in the villages at the time of the attack or right after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you can remember, the houses that were destroyed, did the destruction start from below or from above? As a policeman, what would you say about the origin of the destruction? And another question: When you entered the houses, did you see traces of fire, given your expert eye, in police terms, were you able to observe certain things? A policeman would usually observe certain things if he entered a house that was destroyed. So what sort of conclusions did you draw upon entering these houses as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Like I earlier mentioned, there were 631 destroyed buildings that we recorded, and I would say that, you know, pretty much all of those houses, they were their own cases. There were some of the buildings with only the -- some couple of stones left and some of the houses which had, you know, there was a roof missing, or there was one wall missing that had been hammered down, or it has been burnt. You can see that it has been on fire inside the whole building. The roof has collapsed, if it has not burned. It's difficult to say whether it started from below or high, because each of those buildings, they are their own cases, and there's no kind of, you know, kind of like a typical case. They were all more or less destroyed in different ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A minute ago you said that your instructions were not to concern yourself with buildings in which there were only light traces of bullets. The buildings that had been destroyed, did they have any holes in the walls caused by bullets? Did they give you the impression that machine-guns had opened fire on these houses? And did you notice any cartridges or bullets that remained there? The sort of things that an ordinary policeman would notice? Did you notice that the fire had been opened on any of these buildings?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. Definitely there were some houses which had bullet holes and had been destroyed, but also there were buildings which didn't carry any visible bullet holes. And when you asked about the cartridges and bullets, you have to keep in mind that it's almost ten years at the time and the nature has kind of taken over. There's grass growing everywhere. But still there are some cartridges found from the buildings, or nearby. But I think that's pretty much the case in all over Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you entered these houses in large settlements where there were inhabitants, did some people come to you spontaneously to talk to you, to ask you what you were doing there? Was there ever such a situation, or did no one ever come to see you? Because you said that you yourself never went to see people, but did the people come to see and speak to you?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes. There were some people who approached me. They approached this contact person because I think he's a really well-known person in that area, and like I mentioned earlier, that he had been going around there. So the villagers knew exactly what he was after and he had told that the following month he will come with the OTP personnel to record the damage to the villages, and some people were just curious to see that, you know, what we were doing, and then they had been refugees and returned to the village. But like I said earlier, I didn't start taking any notes from them because this contact person had already kind of like identified potential witnesses to testify about them and the plan was to take the statements during the following mission that we had been planning for June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people who came to see -- did they give you the impression of being victims, of being vindictive, of wanting information on the future indemnities that they might receive? What sort of impression did they leave you and speak to Mr. X or your interpreter? Is there anything that you noticed on such occasions?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember anything special regarding that matter. Most of the time they were just offering us coffee or tea and, you know, chatting about everything possible, and probably also touching the events, what happened there and what was the -- most of the time they wanted to tell their own story and they escaped and what their family is doing and children doing and this kind of thing. It's more like a social conversation most of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You spoke to them, since you say that while having coffee they would talk to you and tell you their personal background. So on that occasion, did they tell you that they were there in 1993 and when X, Y, or Z arrived, they were there? Did they give you any specific details about what had happened at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that you took over 2.000 photographs of the houses. I have to say that we don't have these photographs. Wasn't it possible to put these photographs into binders with references, with the name of the owner of the house, the date when the house was built? I believe that all this is contained on a CD-ROM, but there are no photos, no files that were made, which is what is done in your country and in all countries throughout the world.

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yes. At a certain stage we discussed about the issue of these ground photographs that were taken from the destroyed houses, and at some higher level a decision was made that we will not -- we would just keep them as CD-ROMs, and if needed, they will be used after some later stage. But the main purpose was to kind of present the damage to the villages through the aerial photographs, and we were kind of, you know, concentrating on preparing them. And one thing was that I was just about to leave the Tribunal before we get them finished, and I don't really know what's the story of the other photographs after I left the Tribunal in September 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A while ago the Prosecution showed you photographs of these places using Sanction. We have all noted that you had blue or red markers for houses, and there were numbers. We noticed that at times there were houses that had been destroyed. And there were also houses in a perfect condition. And then next to these houses, a house in good condition. When looking at the photograph, we have the impression that the destruction wasn't systematic, that a selection may have been made when these buildings were destroyed. You, who were at the site, what did you -- what conclusion did you draw when you saw that certain houses had not been destroyed? Are there any explanations you could provide us with on the basis of what you were personally able to observe there?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: This is also an issue that I was thinking about, that how come, you know, some houses were left intact, while the others in surrounding area, they were all destroyed. And I don't have any straight answers. I was just thinking about that maybe there were some -- even though the owner of the house was a Croat, he probably was a certain kind of, you know, person that the people who attacked the village probably knew and didn't want to destroy, for reason or other. I don't know exactly what was that, what was the reason for that. But I've been thinking about the same as well, what was the criteria for selecting the houses, which were destroyed and which were left. I don't have any clear answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having been at the site and on the basis of what you observed as a policeman, the destruction such as depicted in the photographs, is this destruction -- could happen at a given time, in a brief time, or is it necessary to have a number of days or a number of weeks to commit such destruction? As a policeman, what would your comments be as far as the time it took to have destruction of such an extent? As an expert, do you have a point of view about the amount of time that was required in order to destroy these houses?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Again you're asking something which is really difficult to say. It depends on the number of troops which are attacking the village, how many soldiers there are or whatever persons they are who attack and make the destruction. It can be done -- it can be done pretty quickly as well. There are some witnesses who said that there were many, many houses burned during the same night; for example, in Guca Gora, four, five, if I remember correctly. And also other damage has been done to the houses. So it's really difficult to say. Of course, when you talk about some small village, it's much easier and quicker to do the job compared to some larger areas like Grahovcici or Cukle. But of course when you talk about bigger villages, I would guess that there would also be a bigger number of soldiers attacking those villages. So it's like a line drawn to the water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, as a policeman, you are making a link between the extent of destruction and the number of houses and the number of troops that may have destroyed the houses. So you're establishing a link between these elements, these factors. You are saying that in a small village, in which there are two or three houses, only one person could destroy them, but in a large settlement, where there were tens of houses, just one person couldn't destroy them. This would have to be done by a number of troops. This is what you are telling us as an investigator?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah, basically. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will now move on to another subject that isn't directly linked to the subject of destruction but has to do with your role as an investigator. Yesterday, when examining a witness, we realised that your name was mentioned in archives -- in archival material that was provided to the Prosecution, when the Prosecution went to the archives in Sarajevo. They went to the -- to visit the archives of the BH army. Do you remember having been present during this stage when documents were being collected? Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Yeah. I have taken part in such kind of mission, but I'm not able to even recall which year it was. Probably 2001 or 2000. I'm not exactly sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are confirming that you went to the office where there were military documents, to the department where military documents were kept, and on that occasion you took originals or copies? Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: I worked in one or two archives in Bosnia, and we took the originals with us, after we had located them from the binders or from the shelves. We took the originals, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my question overlaps, or the questions I asked you a minute ago. As far as the archives are concerned, did you have from the OTP any guidelines concerning the nature of the documents you were to take, any guidelines concerning the criteria of reliability for these documents, or did you just go to the archives and take whatever you got hold of? Had all of this been prepared in a scientific and professional manner, or were you told: Go to the archives and see what might be of interest. Take what you think might be of interest. Could you provide us with any clarifications?

utterances.speaker: MIKA TAURU
utterances.text: Well, when we went to the archives, there was a clear kind of, you know, areas and time frames and certain units and certain persons that we were interested in, and we had prepared a list - I think was it one or two pages - of all the keywords and key incidents that we were interested in, in our investigations.
